newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa Q2 oper income up on higher volume.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa Q2 oper income up on higher volume.

text.p: Aluminum Co of Amercia said Monday that operating income in the second quarter, ended June 30, climbed to $424.0 million, compared with $350.1 million in the 1996 second quarter.

The company attributed the increase in operating earnings to higher volume and lower controllable expenses. Alcoa added that prices improved from first quarter 1997 levels but remained lower than those in the second quarter of 1996.
The company made the comments upon releasing second quarter earnings Monday. Net earnings were $207.6 million, or $1.19 per share, vs $132.2 million, or $0.76 per share, in the year-earlier period.

Alcoa also said that earnings were hurt in the 1996 second-quarter by an after tax writedown on the value of some aluminum contracts of $33.8 million, or $0.19 a share. In the 1997 second quarter those writedowns fell to $7.1 million or $0.04 per share.
Earnings in the 1996 half were also hurt by a $40 million charge for the shutdown of ceramic packaging operations, said the company.
Currency translation and exchange adjustments reduced net income in the first half of 1997 by $2.8 million, but aided results in the year-earlier period by $3.5 million.

Aluminum shipments, said the company, were 760,000 metric tons (mt) for the 1997 second quarter, compared with 721,000 mt in the year-ago quarter. During the 1997 first half, shipments were 1,480,000 tonnes, compared with 1,377,000 tonnes in the 1996 period.
